AEIS is a direct RF/plasma-power and precision-control candidate; verify whether leading-edge AI logic/memory process complexity is increasing content per tool.
ICHR is a narrower and more underfollowed fluid-delivery subsystem candidate with high OEM customer concentration; this concentration is both a validation signal and a Layer 2 risk.
Layer 2 should add UCTT, ENTG, and possibly non-US-listed VAT Group and INFICON as peer checks, but they were excluded from this Layer 1B output to keep the candidate list at four.

The strongest version of the node thesis is not simply 'more WFE'; it is rising subsystem intensity per process step, driven by tighter tolerances in etch, deposition, advanced packaging, and leading-edge memory/logic.

MKSI should remain a high-priority underfollowed candidate for semicap tool subsystems because its vacuum, photonics, process-control and materials divisions map directly to the node; later layers must verify revenue mix, OEM/customer exposure and debt-risk impact.
AEIS maps cleanly to the RF/plasma/high-voltage power portion of the node; later layers should separate semiconductor-equipment power exposure from data-center and industrial power exposure.
ICHR is the smallest and most underfollowed of this pass, with direct gas/chemical delivery subsystem relevance but likely higher customer concentration and cycle risk.

For this node, the best research path is to use LRCX/AMAT/ASML/KLA/TEL as tool-OEM demand anchors, then test whether subsystem suppliers have multi-OEM qualification, recurring service/consumables, and pricing power from tight process tolerances.

Need a follow-up search for US-listed or ADR-accessible niche vacuum, metrology, motion-control, valve, flow-control, and inspection suppliers beyond MKSI/AEIS/ICHR; non-US names such as VAT Group and Inficon appear relevant but were outside the US-listed constraint for this pass.

MKSI should remain in the semicap_tool_subsystems universe despite being above the preferred small/mid-cap range because its exposure appears unusually pure to vacuum, pressure/flow, process-control, and subsystem content in WFE.

ICHR is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for gas, liquid, and chemical delivery subsystems sold to semiconductor capital-equipment OEMs; later layers must verify customer concentration and margin cyclicality.

UCTT is a high-priority underfollowed candidate spanning gas/chemical delivery modules, precision subsystems, and ultra-high-purity cleaning/contamination services; later layers must separate Products versus Services economics.

AEIS, NVMI, COHU, MTSI, ONTO, CAMT, and possibly non-US-listed VAT Group and Inficon are relevant adjacent candidates but were not included in the four-name candidate cap; they should be queued for a follow-up expansion pass.

For this node, the key falsification test is whether subsystem suppliers actually gain content per tool and order growth from advanced-node and AI-related WFE, rather than merely tracking a cyclical rebound in broad semiconductor equipment spending.
MKSI is a high-priority underfollowed subsystem candidate for semicap_tool_subsystems due to vacuum, gas delivery, RF/power, process-control, and advanced packaging/PCB chemistry exposure.
AEIS is a high-priority power-delivery/RF-plasma subsystem candidate; next layer should quantify semiconductor-equipment revenue and OEM design-win durability.
ICHR is the cleanest small/mid-cap direct gas and chemical delivery subsystem candidate, but customer concentration, cyclicality, and margin quality need verification.

node: Semiconductor equipment subsystems: vacuum, RF power, gas flow, measurement, motion control, and process-control components embedded inside larger wafer-fab tools
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around semiconductor-equipment subsystems. The two-lane map uses Applied Materials as a reference OEM/customer anchor, then prioritizes less obvious subsystem suppliers with direct exposure to vacuum/process control, RF/plasma power, and fluid-delivery subsystems. The strongest underfollowed candidates from this pass are MKS Instruments, Advanced Energy Industries, and Ichor Holdings. Key verification work for Layer 2 should focus on segment-level semiconductor exposure, OEM customer concentration, gross-margin durability, backlog/order recovery, and whether AI-driven leading-edge logic, memory, and advanced packaging capex is increasing subsystem intensity rather than merely pulling forward cyclical WFE demand. Expanded the universe around semiconductor equipment subsystems with one obvious wafer-fab-tool reference anchor and three US-listed subsystem/component suppliers. The strongest underfollowed lane names for this node are MKS, Advanced Energy, and Ichor because their products sit inside or adjacent to larger wafer-fab tools: vacuum/process control/specialty chemistry, plasma and high-voltage power, and gas/chemical delivery subsystems. These are second-order AI capex beneficiaries: exposure depends on fab-tool demand, process complexity, and OEM qualification rather than winning end-chip sockets. This Layer 1B pass expands the US-listed universe around semiconductor equipment subsystems.
